chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Abī al-Maghrāʾ, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:

If a boy reaches ten years of age and makes a bequest of one-third of his wealth for a rightful cause, his bequest is valid. And if he is seven years old and bequeaths a small amount of his wealth for a rightful cause, his bequest is valid.

key_terms.الْغُلَامُ: a boy; the minor whose legal bequest is being discussed
key_terms.بِثُلُثِ مَالِهِ: one-third of his property or wealth
key_terms.فِي حَقٍّ: for a rightful and legitimate cause

ai.seo_question: At what age is a child’s bequest considered valid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the validity of a minor boy’s bequest. It states that at ten years old, a bequest of up to one-third of his wealth in a rightful cause is valid, and at seven years old, a bequest of a small amount in a rightful cause is also valid.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5452 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abi Al-Maghra from Abu Baṣir from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), who said:

"If a boy reaches the age of ten and makes a will for one-third of his wealth in a rightful cause, his will is valid. And if he is seven years old and makes a will for a small amount of his wealth in a rightful cause, his will is also valid."
